extracted.intended_audience: Authors, reviewers, editors, and readers of Nature Communications (research scientists and journal staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Journal policy describing mandatory publication of peer review exchanges for research articles submitted from November 2022 onward, plus options for reviewer anonymity/signing, reviewer recognition, and author opt-in double-blind review. It explains the rationale and expected benefits of transparent peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory publication of peer review exchanges for research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: "we are now moving to publish the exchanges between authors and reviewers for all research articles submitted from November 2022 onward and accepted for publication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exchange includes peer reviewers’ comments and authors’ responses published alongside the paper. Rationale given: transparency strengthens the quality of peer review, allows readers to better critically assess the robustness of conclusions, preserves scholarly value of reviews, and benefits both scientists and the public. Historical opt-in data (e.g., ~70% opt-in at Nature Communications prior to this change) is cited as supportive evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers may remain anonymous, sign reports, or be acknowledged by name
rubrics_metrics.description: "Referees will still have the option to remain completely anonymous, to sign their reports, and/or to choose to be acknowledged by name as part of our reviewer recognition scheme."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer choices about identity disclosure remain optional. The policy preserves referee autonomy: they can (a) remain anonymous, (b) sign their reports, and/or (c) opt into being named via the reviewer recognition scheme. The editorial emphasizes gratitude for reviewers’ time and intent to respect their preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recognition scheme (optional acknowledgement)
rubrics_metrics.description: "...to choose to be acknowledged by name as part of our reviewer recognition scheme."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing peer review files can provide greater recognition to reviewers who wish to be acknowledged for their contribution. Participation in recognition is voluntary and separate from the option to sign individual reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors may opt into double-blind peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: "We will also continue to offer our authors the possibility to opt-in double blind peer-review, during which their identities remain anonymous to the referees during the review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain the option to request double-blind handling so that referees do not see author identities during review; this choice does not affect the post-acceptance publication of the peer review file (the policy to publish exchanges applies to accepted research articles submitted from Nov 2022 onward).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and limits of peer review as an evaluative standard
rubrics_metrics.description: "The evaluation of scientific studies by peers prior to their publication is an important tool to ensure that widely disseminated science adheres to sufficiently rigorous standards of proof, and that the reported findings are adequately interpreted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is presented as improving reliability of early results and the overall value of manuscripts, but it cannot completely guarantee validity — especially when competing hypotheses exist. Making peer review exchanges public helps readers judge robustness, reveals where authors and referees disagreed (valid caveats/limitations), and lets authors surface arguments that cannot be integrated into the paper narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review comments as scholarly record to be preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: "Amongst the listed benefits of an open review process, the idea that the peer review comments represent valuable scholarship that should be preserved is one we particularly agree with."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial stance that peer review reports are valuable scholarship and should be part of the official scientific record; publishing them preserves these discussions for future readers and researchers.
